body:
Fixes two role-model bugs the human met after Agent Roles (2026-11-05). A role's model is only the starting value of the model picker; it does not decide which model an action runs.

### What changes
- A role's model fills the model picker when a task opens or its column changes. A model picked by hand stays until the task changes or that model can no longer start.
- Changing a role's model in Settings reaches open pickers immediately, without a page reload or reopening the task.
- Investigate, Assign, Review and the other task actions send the model currently shown in the picker, with its effort. They no longer substitute the action's own role default.
- A picker with no role default keeps its existing "Select a model" behavior.

### Acceptance criteria
- With a role set to model B, an open task whose picker follows that role starts on B; clicking Assign sends the model now selected in the picker, not the action's role default.
- After a role's model changes in Settings, an open task picker and an open Strategy plan picker show the new default without a reload, unless someone picked a model by hand.
- Actions use the selected model and effort.
- Focused tests cover: the default filling the picker, a live default change reaching both pages, a hand pick staying, and actions sending the selected model.
- Existing tests that assert an action uses its own role's default are updated to the new behavior.

### For the agent
`solace_task.action_choice` is where an action swaps in its own role's default; `solace_task.refresh` already re-fetches role models. `strategy.choose_plan_model` does the same for the plan. A change made in Settings must reach both elements while they stay mounted and hidden.

### Out of scope
Changing role definitions, skills, Autorun, and the model list itself.
title: Agent roles: default fills picker only
